Header: Citrus blight, citrus tristeza (CTV) and Phytophthora soil diseases, e.g. P. citrophthora

Prevention: Adopt scheduled and technically viable methods of irrigation.
Use healthy root stocks for plantation.
Maintain pH of the soil between 5.5-7.5 by adopting balanced agricultural practices and fertilizers.
Level the soil and pay attention to better soil drainage.
Select the citrus varieties suited to agroecological environment.
Control the weeds manually or with chemicals as they serve as alternate hosts for insect pests and diseases and also compete with citrus for nutrients.
NPK and other micronutrients in balanced proportion.
Monitoring: In early stages of the disease, symptoms are restricted to a few twigs but eventually the whole tree is affected with sparse foliage mottled leaves and stunted growth.
Carefully observe the yellowing of older leaves and drying up of the twigs.
Plants affected by decline also exhibit excessive flowering but produce weak small-sized fruits.
The fruits also have thick skin, are undesirably firm and lack in gloss with many skin blemishes.

Also keenly observe the factors causing decline e.g. soil pH, salt status, soil structure, low organic matter, presence of a hard core, nutrient deficiency, incompatible root stock and attack of insect pests and diseases, etc.
Direct Control: The only control is to remove the affected tree and replace with more tolerant rootstocks.
Spray neem oil @ 5 ml/litre or other organic pesticides for insect pest and diseases.
Apply dolomite lime powder @ 3kg/tree in alternate year.
Restrictions: Bordeaux paste on the tree (up to 60 cm height from ground level).
